instrument: Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulation Act 2001
text_verbatim: The Commission may, for the purpose of ensuring continuity of telecommunication services in an emergency, issue directions to an operator regarding the operation, restoration and prioritisation of its telecommunication system, and the operator shall comply with such directions.

instrument: Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulation Act 2001
text_verbatim: The Government may, in the interest of the security of the State or public order, direct the suspension or interception of telecommunication services, and any such direction shall be issued by the authority empowered by the Government for that purpose.

instrument: BTRC international roaming directive (Bangladesh)
text_verbatim: An operator shall not provide or alter international roaming arrangements, including arrangements with operators of a neighbouring country, except with the prior written approval of the Commission, and any request for such approval shall be processed in accordance with the Commission's standard timelines.

instrument: Cyclone Preparedness Programme standing order (Bangladesh)
text_verbatim: The Cyclone Preparedness Programme shall disseminate cyclone warning signals issued by the Bangladesh Meteorological Department to coastal communities through its network of volunteers using megaphones, flags and sirens, in Bengali, and shall continue dissemination until the danger signal is withdrawn.

instrument: Disaster Management Act 2012 (Bangladesh)
text_verbatim: The National Disaster Management Council shall approve national disaster management policies and plans, and the Department of Disaster Management shall coordinate the dissemination of early warnings for impending disasters to the population of the areas likely to be affected, in Bengali.

instrument: Disaster Management Act 2012 (Bangladesh)
text_verbatim: On receipt of an early warning of an impending disaster, the Deputy Commissioner of the district concerned shall activate the district disaster management committee and shall cause the warning to be disseminated to the inhabitants of the areas likely to be affected through all available means without delay.

instrument: Bangladesh National Emergency Telecommunication Service (NETS) initiative
text_verbatim: NEGATIVE FINDING, not a quotation. An initiative for a national emergency telecommunication service has existed since September 2022, but as reported no plan had been put in place and allocated funds remained unused. Cited as a neighbouring-country instance of the absence of a national emergency telecommunication plan in practice.

instrument: Bangladesh Standing Orders on Disaster (SOD) 2019
section: Posts and Telecommunications Division / BTRC / BTCL responsibilities (pp. 240-246)
text_verbatim: The Posts and Telecommunications Division, the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission and BTCL are assigned responsibilities for maintaining and restoring telecommunication services during a disaster, including keeping emergency communication available to the disaster management authorities. Page range per the SOD table of contents; extract and quote the actual pages before citing.

instrument: Bhutan Standard Operating Procedure for Telecommunication Services during Disaster
text_verbatim: NEGATIVE FINDING, not a quotation. Bhutan's SOP for telecommunication services during disaster contains no provision for roaming between operators, sets no numeric response timelines, and requires daily reporting expressed as 'immediately' rather than against a measured deadline. Cited as a neighbouring-country comparator for the absence of a standing roaming trigger.

instrument: CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6) IT Act, 28 April 2022 (India)
text_verbatim: Any service provider, intermediary, data centre, body corporate and Government organisation shall mandatorily report cyber incidents of the types specified in Annexure I to CERT-In within six hours of noticing such incidents or being brought to notice about such incidents.

instrument: CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6) IT Act, 28 April 2022 (India)
text_verbatim: All service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporate and Government organisations shall mandatorily enable logs of all their ICT systems and maintain them securely for a rolling period of 180 days within the Indian jurisdiction, and these shall be provided to CERT-In along with reporting of any incident or when ordered or directed by CERT-In.

instrument: Disaster Management Act 2005 (India)
text_verbatim: The State Executive Committee shall give directions to any department of the Government of the State or any other authority or body in the State regarding actions to be taken in response to any threatening disaster situation or disaster, and shall advise the State Government regarding all financial matters in relation to disaster management.

instrument: Disaster Management Act 2005 (India)
text_verbatim: The District Authority shall ensure that communication systems are in order and that disaster management drills are carried out periodically, and shall, in the event of a disaster, provide information to the State Authority relating to different aspects of disaster management.

instrument: Disaster Management Act 2005 (India)
text_verbatim: For the purpose of assisting and protecting the community affected by a disaster, the District Authority may give directions for the release and use of resources available with any department of the Government and the local authority in the district, and may ensure that warnings and alerts are communicated to the public in the affected area.

instrument: Disaster Management Act 2005 (India)
text_verbatim: Whoever, without reasonable cause, obstructs any officer or employee of the Government or a person authorised by the Authority in the discharge of their functions under this Act, or refuses to comply with any direction given by or on behalf of the Government or the Authority under this Act, shall on conviction be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine, or with both.

instrument: Disaster Management Act 2005 (India)
text_verbatim: The National Disaster Management Authority shall have the responsibility for laying down the policies, plans and guidelines for disaster management and for coordinating their enforcement and implementation throughout the country, and shall lay down guidelines to be followed by the departments or agencies of the Government of India.

instrument: DoT Standard Operating Procedure 2020 for Telecommunication Services for responding to Disasters (India)
text_verbatim: A national committee chaired by Member (Technology) oversees telecom disaster response, with corresponding committees at licensed service area (circle) level, nodal officers designated by each telecom service provider, and damage-assessment teams. Content per secondary reporting; verify against the SOP before quoting.

instrument: DoT Standard Operating Procedure 2020 for Telecommunication Services for responding to Disasters (India)
text_verbatim: Intra-circle roaming during a disaster is to be arranged through mutual agreement between telecom service providers, pursuant to memoranda of understanding entered into between them, rather than by a standing regulatory trigger. Activation is requested through the designated DoT disaster official. Dated 14 December 2020. Content per secondary reporting; verify against the SOP before quoting.

instrument: IMD Cyclone Warning Services standard operating procedure (India)
text_verbatim: The India Meteorological Department issues cyclone warnings in four stages: Pre-Cyclone Watch, Cyclone Alert, Cyclone Warning, and Post-Landfall Outlook, addressed to the State Governments and disaster management authorities of the areas likely to be affected, with the Cyclone Warning stage issued at least twenty-four hours before expected commencement of adverse weather.

instrument: NDMA Common Alerting Protocol / SACHET Integrated Alert System (India)
text_verbatim: The Common Alerting Protocol based Integrated Alert System disseminates disaster warnings issued by designated alerting authorities to the public in the affected area over multiple channels including cell broadcast and SMS, in English, Hindi and the relevant regional language, with the alerting authority responsible for the area accountable for issuing the alert.

instrument: Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: Directions to suspend telecommunication services shall not be issued except by an order made by the Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Home Affairs in the case of the Central Government, or by the Secretary to the State Government in charge of the Home Department in the case of a State Government, who is hereby designated as the competent authority.

instrument: Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: In unavoidable circumstances where obtaining prior direction of the competent authority is not feasible, such direction may be issued by an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary to the Government of India who has been duly authorised by the competent authority, and such direction shall cease to be in effect unless confirmed by the competent authority within twenty-four hours of its issue.

instrument: Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: Every order issued directing suspension of telecommunication services shall contain reasons for such direction, shall specify the area and duration of suspension, and a copy of such order shall be forwarded to the concerned Review Committee not later than the next working day.

instrument: Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: Any direction for suspension of telecommunication services shall not remain in operation for more than fifteen days at a time, and a fresh order shall be required to continue the suspension beyond that period.

instrument: Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: The Review Committee shall meet within five working days of the issue of a direction for suspension of telecommunication services and shall record its findings on whether the direction is in accordance with the governing provisions of law.

instrument: Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: The authorised entity shall designate a nodal officer in each licensed service area to receive and handle directions for suspension of telecommunication services, and no direction shall be acted upon unless it is received through the designated nodal officer channel.

instrument: Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: NEGATIVE FINDING, not a quotation. The Telecom Cyber Security Rules 2024 impose incident-reporting duties on authorised entities but, on secondary reporting of the notified text, contain no requirement that an authorised entity authenticate the provenance of a direction or order received from a government officer before giving effect to it. This record exists so the policy engine can cite the absence of such a duty. It must be confirmed against the full notified text before the report asserts it.

instrument: Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules 2024 (India)
text_verbatim: An authorised entity shall report a telecom cyber security incident affecting its telecommunication network or telecommunication service to the Central Government within six hours of becoming aware of such incident, and shall furnish detailed information in respect of the incident within twenty-four hours of such report. Notified 21 November 2024. Content per secondary reporting; verify against the eGazette notification before quoting.

instrument: Unified Licence, Department of Telecommunications (India)
text_verbatim: The Licensee shall make provision for monitoring and for making its network available for disaster relief, shall comply with directions issued by the Licensor in respect of emergency and disaster situations, and shall provide intra-circle or inter-operator roaming facilities where so directed by the Licensor.

instrument: GSMA guidance on mobile network operator disaster response
text_verbatim: Where national regulation permits, operators may implement disaster roaming so that subscribers of an operator whose radio access network is unavailable in a disaster-affected area can register on a surviving network, subject to pre-agreed technical arrangements and a defined trigger and termination condition.

instrument: Constitution of the International Telecommunication Union
text_verbatim: International telecommunication services must accord absolute priority to all telecommunications concerning safety of life at sea, on land, in the air or in outer space, as well as to epidemiological telecommunications of exceptional urgency of the World Health Organization.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation E.106, International Emergency Preference Scheme for disaster relief operations
text_verbatim: The International Emergency Preference Scheme provides for priority treatment of calls made by authorised personnel engaged in disaster relief operations, including priority in call set-up and preferential access to network resources, to be applied by network operators on the basis of authorisation granted by the responsible national authority.

instrument: ITU-D Guidelines for National Emergency Telecommunication Plans (2020)
text_verbatim: The ITU guidelines set out how a country should develop a national emergency telecommunication plan covering preparedness, response and recovery for telecommunication networks, and reflect the ITU objective that every country have such a plan in place. Cited as the global benchmark against which a national SOP is compared.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation Q.3057 (signature-based calling party identity authentication)
text_verbatim: ITU-T standardises certificate-based authentication of calling party identity in signalling, providing a signed-identity mechanism and the supporting protocol and certificate-management procedures. Cited to show that ITU already standardises cryptographically signed identity in telecommunication signalling, while no analogous mechanism exists for authenticating a government direction issued to an operator.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation X.1303, Common Alerting Protocol (CAP 1.1)
text_verbatim: The Common Alerting Protocol provides an open, non-proprietary digital message format for all types of alerts and notifications, specifying an alert message structure with alert, info, resource and area blocks, where the info block carries the language, category, urgency, severity and certainty of the alert and the area block carries the geographic scope.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation Y.3172, Architectural framework for machine learning in future networks including IMT-2020
text_verbatim: The machine learning pipeline is a set of logical nodes, each with specific functionalities, that can be combined to form a machine learning application. The nodes comprise SRC (source), C (collector), PP (pre-processor), M (model), P (policy), D (distributor) and SINK, where the policy node applies constraints on the output of the model node before it is applied to the network.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation Y.3173, Framework for evaluating intelligence levels of future networks including IMT-2020
text_verbatim: The framework evaluates the intelligence level of a network across dimensions including monitoring, analysis, decision and execution, where higher levels correspond to a greater degree of autonomous decision making and lower levels retain human involvement in the decision and execution steps.

instrument: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030
text_verbatim: To invest in, develop, maintain and strengthen people-centred multi-hazard, multisectoral forecasting and early warning systems, disaster risk and emergency communications mechanisms, social technologies and hazard-monitoring telecommunications systems, and to develop such systems through a participatory process, tailoring them to the needs of users, including social and cultural requirements, in particular gender.

instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
text_verbatim: The States Parties shall cooperate among themselves and with non-State entities and intergovernmental organizations to facilitate the use of telecommunication resources for disaster mitigation and relief, including the deployment of terrestrial and satellite telecommunication equipment to predict, monitor and provide information concerning natural hazards and disasters. Party status of individual States must be verified on the UN Treaty Collection before being encoded in a policy pack (see spec section 14).

instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
text_verbatim: A State Party requiring telecommunication assistance for disaster mitigation and relief may request such assistance from any other State Party, and the requested State Party shall promptly determine and notify the requesting State Party whether it will render the assistance requested, directly or otherwise, and the scope of and terms on which such assistance might be rendered.

instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
text_verbatim: States Parties shall, where possible and in conformity with their national law, reduce or remove regulatory barriers to the use of telecommunication resources for disaster mitigation and relief, including barriers relating to the licensing of the use of allocated frequencies, restrictions on the import of equipment, limitations on the movement of humanitarian teams, and restrictions on roaming and the use of telecommunication resources across borders.

instrument: 47 CFR 4.17 — Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (United States)
text_verbatim: Facilities-based mobile wireless providers shall, when the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative is triggered, provide reasonable roaming under disaster arrangements to requesting providers where technically feasible, so that subscribers of a provider whose network is impaired in the affected area can obtain service on another provider's network.

instrument: 47 CFR 4.17 — Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (United States)
text_verbatim: Participating providers shall engage in mutual aid during emergencies, including enhanced municipal preparedness and restoration coordination, and shall provide a single point of contact for public safety entities in the affected area for the duration of the event.

instrument: 47 CFR 4.17 — Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (United States)
text_verbatim: The obligations of the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative are triggered automatically upon activation of the Disaster Information Reporting System for an area, without the need for a separate order from the Commission directed at each provider.

instrument: 47 CFR Part 4 -- Disruptions to Communications (United States)
text_verbatim: Wireless service providers shall submit electronically a notification to the Commission within 120 minutes of discovering an outage that potentially affects a 911 special facility, and shall submit an initial outage report within 72 hours and a final report within 30 days of discovering the outage.

instrument: FCC Disaster Information Reporting System (United States)
text_verbatim: When the Disaster Information Reporting System is activated for a geographic area, communications providers in that area are directed to report the operational status of their infrastructure, including cell sites out of service and switches down, on a daily basis for the duration of the activation.

instrument: FCC Wireless Emergency Alerts rules (United States)
text_verbatim: Participating Commercial Mobile Service providers shall support transmission of Wireless Emergency Alerts in English and Spanish, and shall transmit alerts received from the Alert Gateway to the geographic area specified by the alert originator.
